notes:
Your books get a cast.

Novels used to be read in one flat voice for hours — the story and the talking sounded like the same person. Now they don't. The split is read straight from the quotation marks the writer typed, so it's right whenever the writing is, and there's a breath where the voice changes.

Turn it up to CAST in Settings and lines the writing actually attributes — “she said” — get a voice to match. Anything it can't be sure of keeps the ordinary speaking voice rather than guessing.

Books also open where you stopped. Continue used to restart the chapter from the top, which on a long chapter threw away most of a sitting.

And on one source that serves its text with the apostrophes stripped out, the narrator was saying “ill” for “I'll” and “wont” for “won't”. Fixed.
